endpoint.text: The trial assessed two primary endpoints: change from baseline in serum oligosaccharide levels (a biomarker) and change from baseline in the 3-minute stair climbing test (3MSCT), assessed at 12 months; key secondary endpoints were the 6MWT and FVC % predicted.

citations.quote: The single adequate and well-controlled clinical trial in the velmanase development program, Trial rhLAMAN-05, assessed two primary endpoints, the change from baseline in a biomarker, serum oligosaccharide levels, and the change from baseline in a clinical endpoint, the 3MSCT, as well as two key secondary endpoints, the 6MWT and FVC%.

The efficacy results for the clinical endpoints assessed at 12 months, 3-minute stair climbing test (3MSCT), 6-minute walking test (6MWT) and forced vital capacity (FVC) (% predicted), favored the LAMZEDE group and were supported by a reduction in serum oligosaccharide concentration. The results of 3MSCT, 6MWT, FVC (% predicted), and serum oligosaccharide concentrations are presented in Table 2.
Fifteen patients (8 adult and 7 pediatric) received LAMZEDE and 10 patients (5 adult and 5 pediatric) received placebo. All patients completed the trial.

result.text: 3MSCT mean relative change +0.5% (LAMZEDE) vs -3.6% (placebo), treatment difference 3.4% (95% CI -9.5, 16.3); FVC % predicted absolute change +8.2 vs +2.0, difference 5.5 (95% CI -5.0, 16.1); serum oligosaccharides relative change -75.8% vs -20.3%, difference -55.6% (95% CI -69.3, -41.9).

citations.quote: Velmanase alfa (velmanase) is a new molecular entity recombinant human alpha-mannosidase that functions as an ERT for the endogenous enzyme that is deficient in AM. Velmanase is internalized by cells and transported to the lysosomes where it functions as the endogenous enzyme.
Alpha-mannosidase normally catalyzes the degradation of accumulated mannose-containing oligosaccharides in various tissues.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >20%) are hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis, nasopharyngitis (66% vs 70% placebo), pyrexia (40% vs 50%), headache (33% vs 30%), and arthralgia (20% vs 10%). In clinical trials 19 (50%) LAMZEDE-treated patients experienced hypersensitivity reactions, including 2 (5%) with anaphylaxis.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: SEVERE HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTIONS

Patients treated with LAMZEDE have experienced hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis. Appropriate medical support measures, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation equipment, should be readily available during LAMZEDE administration. If a severe hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis) occurs, discontinue LAMZEDE immediately and initiate appropriate medical treatment.

summary.text: LAMZEDE (velmanase alfa-tycv) was approved via the traditional approval pathway under a Priority Review as an enzyme replacement therapy for alpha-mannosidosis. It held Orphan Drug designation (granted February 2, 2006), Rare Pediatric Disease designation (granted December 11, 2018), and Fast Track designation (granted December 12, 2019). Efficacy was established with one adequate and well-controlled trial (rhLAMAN-05) plus confirmatory mechanistic evidence.

citations.quote: This application met the criteria for a priority review because velmanase treats a serious condition for which there is currently no approved treatment, and if approved, would provide a significant improvement in effectiveness in treatment of AM.
Velmanase received orphan designation in February 2006, rare pediatric designation in December 2018, and Fast Track Designation in December 2019.
A Rare Pediatric Disease designation was granted for velmanase on December 11, 2018.
Substantial evidence of effectiveness for velmanase alfa in AM patients was established with one adequate and well-controlled trial with confirmatory evidence.
